title: Tom White's letter to Central Casting for Spikes
summary: Spikes shows a letter from Tom White of the Hollywood Recording Company recommending him to Central Casting; he declined the job.

blocks.x:
Jazz Oral History Project
Interview with Benjamin "Reb" Spikes
Conducted by Patricia Willard
Cassette 4
He didn't put a date on it--unfortunately.
Well, I don't know what day it was. It was a...
You found here this letter written by Tom White at the Hollywood Recording Company. You said that he was the man that made the Chinese picture. Is that right?
Yeah, he made a picture with Chinese...

And he has written on his letterhead of The Hollywood Recording Company, 6276 Hollywood Boulevard--which would be right about Hollywood and Ivar--but we don't have the date on it. It says, uh, "Recording at 33 1/3 or 80 RPM," and he had "Studio Space, Sound Effects, Recording Orchestras," and the note is addressed to Dave Allen at Central Casting:
"Dear Dave:
"The bearer, Reb Spikes, is a friend of mine, and I will appreciate anything you can do for him. He is honest, reliable, and trustworthy.
"Thanks.

"Regards,

"Tom White"

And that was the job at Central Casting which you didn't want. Right?
Well, I didn't want to take it away from the other boy.
That would have been approximately what year?
Oh, I think it was...uh, between '25 and '30--somewhere in there.
